target_game.name: Push'em all
target_game.core_loop: Swipe to move the character, use an expanding stick to push crowds of enemies off the platform, and reach the end of the level.
target_game.audience_proxy: Casual gamers of all ages looking for simple, satisfying, and quick action-oriented gameplay sessions.
target_game.visual_style: Minimalist 3D with bright, contrasting colors and simple stickman-like figures.

palette.description: Vibrant blue water and green/sandy platforms contrasted sharply by bright red enemy figures.

game_fit_scores.rationale: Mechanic mismatch is the dealbreaker: rapid-fire grid-block placement is a puzzle/Tetris-style satisfaction loop with zero overlap with Push'em All's swipe-to-shove crowd physics — recreating this hook would misrepresent the product and tank IPM/retention. Palette also clashes (green/blue/yellow puzzle tones vs. our signature red-vs-blue stickman contrast), and there's no character or platform action to anchor it. Audience is the only partial bridge (broad hypercasual satisfaction-seekers), but not enough to justify production; skip this archetype or, at most, borrow the "SMART GENIUS PSYCHOPATH" escalating-text overlay device on top of native push gameplay.

Hard pass: a Goku/Ultra Instinct anime transformation hook has zero connection to Push'em All's stickman crowd-pushing loop, and using licensed DBZ IP creates serious legal/ASA takedown risk that outweighs any CTR upside. The palette overlaps loosely on blue, but the anime rendering style clashes with the game's flat minimalist 3D, and while shonen fans skew casual-mobile, they expect RPG/gacha combat — bounce/uninstall rates would be brutal. Skip this archetype; if the team wants the "transformation" emotional beat, recreate it natively with the in-game "SIZE UP!" power-up moment instead.

Hard pass for Push'em All. The Dragon Ball anime aesthetic (gold/orange/navy, detailed character animation, shonen power-fantasy framing) clashes with the game's minimalist 3D stickman look and bright blue/green/red palette, and a charged-fist anime attack does not communicate the swipe-to-push crowd-control loop at all. Audience also skews older/male anime-fan rather than the broad all-ages hypercasual base, plus there's obvious IP risk using Goku — do not greenlight, even as a stylistic reference.

The hypercasual "relaxing satisfaction" audience overlaps strongly with Push'em All's broad casual base, but the hook itself is fundamentally mismatched: traffic-jam puzzle solving is slow/cerebral while Push'em All's value prop is energetic crowd-pushing physics chaos — there's no honest way to bait this hook and deliver the actual game without a bounce. Palette and stylus-on-vehicles visuals also clash with the stickman-on-platform 3D look. Recommend skipping a direct adaptation; if testing, only borrow the "have you played a game that..." VO framing over native push-crowds-off-platform footage rather than replicating the traffic-jam hook.

Hard pass for Push'em All. The archetype's muted slate/khaki/teal palette and realistic landmark cross-section animation are stylistically incompatible with the game's bright primary-color, stickman-on-a-platform identity — viewers clicking this hook expect a base-builder/exploration/narrative experience, not a swipe-and-push hypercasual. Audience overlap is only mildly present (broad casual mobile users skew curiosity-driven), but the mechanic delta is severe: there is no plausible 3-second pivot from a subterranean bunker reveal into crowd-pushing physics without catastrophic IPM drop and likely policy/misleading-ad risk. Recommend not adapting this archetype; if curiosity-cross-section must be tested, restage it as a "what's under the platform?" reveal showing water/sharks below the stickman arena instead.

brief.title: Smart. Genius. Psychopath. — Push'em All Edition
brief.hook_3s: A blue stickman's stick EXPANDS and sweeps 30 red enemies off the platform in one satisfying physics ragdoll wave — splash, splash, splash.
scene_flow: 0-3s: Tight top-down on the blue platform. Player swipes once, stick expands modestly, shoves a small red cluster off the edge. Overlay: 'SMART'.
3-7s: Camera pulls back. Bigger swipe, 'SIZE UP!' power-up triggers, stick doubles in length, wipes a full row of red stickmen into the water in a single arc. Overlay: 'GENIUS'.

7-12s: Combo multiplier x8 spikes on HUD, coin counter ticks up rapidly, level timeline fills. Stick grows absurdly long, sweeping a 50-enemy crowd off a narrow bridge — ragdolls splash in slow-mo. Overlay: 'PSYCHOPATH'.
12-15s: Final boss-platform: one mega-swipe clears everything, level-complete burst, coins rain. CTA card snaps in.
brief.visual_direction: Lock to the native Push'em All look: vibrant #2a7dfa water, #56a38b sandy/green platforms, bright #e3001b enemy stickmen vs. a blue hero. Minimalist 3D, soft top-down/isometric camera that pulls back as the stick grows. Every escalation beat ends with a bigger red ragdoll splash into blue water — that's the satisfaction payoff. Keep native HUD visible: progress timeline at top, combo multiplier and coin counter, 'SIZE UP!' power-up burst. No filters, no UGC frame — this is pure clean in-game footage with escalating overlays.
brief.rationale: Voodoo's current Push'em All rotation is all unlabeled video/playable with no copy hook — there's zero text-driven escalation creative in market. This brief imports the trending 'SMART/GENIUS/PSYCHOPATH' satisfaction-escalation overlay device (the only transferable element from the puzzle archetype) and bolts it onto authentic swipe-and-shove gameplay, giving UA a copy-led variant to A/B against the silent videos without misrepresenting the core loop. Expect lift on CTR via the meme-recognizable text beat while IPM stays protected by truthful gameplay.

brief.title: "Ever Played a Game That…" — POV Push Satisfaction
brief.hook_3s: "Ever played a game that actually makes you feel something?" — phone tilts down to a red stickman crowd getting yeeted into blue water.
scene_flow: 0–3s: Vertical phone-in-hand UGC framing. Casual VO: 'Hey — ever played a game that actually makes you feel something?' Phone screen shows the Push'em All platform with a swarm of red stickmen approaching.
3–7s: Cut to clean in-game POV. Thumb swipes; the blue player extends the stick and sweeps a dense red crowd off the edge — slow-mo splash into water. Combo counter ticks x4, x7, x12.
7–11s: 'SIZE UP!' power-up notification flashes. Stick grows huge, clearing an entire wave in one swing. Coins fountain up. Progress bar surges toward the finish.
11–14s: Quick montage of 3 satisfying push moments — domino chain, edge-of-platform near-miss, final boss crowd wipe.
14–15s: Finish-line confetti, score tally, CTA card snaps in over the gameplay still.

Open with shaky vertical UGC phone-holding framing for authenticity, then cut to crisp top-down-ish gameplay capture with the native HUD intact (progress timeline top, combo multiplier center-screen, coin counter top-right, 'SIZE UP!' burst). Camera punches in on impacts; physics ragdolls exaggerated for the satisfaction payoff.

brief.title: What's Under the Platform? — Cross-Section Reveal for Push'em All
brief.hook_3s: Camera slices through the bright blue water beside the platform — revealing hungry sharks circling directly below the red stickman crowd about to be pushed in.
scene_flow: 0-3s: Top-down hero shot of the sandy platform. Camera tilts and the world splits in half like a diorama — water surface peels away to expose sharks swimming under the arena. Overlay: 'What's down there?'
3-7s: Snap back to gameplay POV. Player swipes, the stick expands, and a red stickman crowd is shoved toward the edge. Combo multiplier ticks up: x2, x3, x4.
7-11s: Cross-section view returns mid-push — we follow a red stickman tumbling off the platform and SPLASH into the shark zone below. Coin counter spikes, 'SIZE UP!' power-up triggers.
11-14s: Wider stick sweeps a massive crowd off in one satisfying arc, level progress bar fills to FINISH.
14-15s: End card with logo, tap-to-play pulse, CTA.
brief.visual_direction: Lean fully into the Push'em All DNA: minimalist 3D, sandy/green platform (#56a38b), vibrant blue water (#2a7dfa), bright red stickman enemies (#e3001b). The 'cross-section' twist is achieved by literally cutting away the water surface to expose a stylized underwater layer — same flat-shaded minimalist 3D, no realism. Keep the energetic/competitive HUD (progress timeline top, combo multiplier center, coin counter top-right). Camera is dynamic: orbiting reveal into top-down gameplay, then a clean diorama split for the payoff. No muted slate/khaki tones from the source archetype — translate the curiosity beat into our bright primary palette.
